samples.summary: Preview subset link can shrink a family that the app shell already loaded in full (Inter / Fraunces / JetBrains Mono from index.html)
samples.evidence: `ensurePreviewFontLink` only refuses to inject a subset when (a) the catalog entry is `eager` (i.e. in `buildGoogleFontsHref`'s bootstrap link) or (b) a wafflebase-injected full link exists (`findFontLink`, line 226). It knows nothing about the *app-shell* stylesheet in `packages/frontend/index.html:12`, which loads `Fraunces`, `Inter` and `JetBrains Mono` in full. All three are curated-catalog entries with no `eager: true` (`font-catalog.data.ts:30`, `:64`, `:66`), so merely scrolling the font dropdown/dialog past the "Inter" row appends `css2?family=Inter:wght@400&text=Inter&display=swap` to `document.head` — declared *after* index.html's link, with no `unicode-range`, so by the author's own cascade reasoning (see the docstring at lines 206-210, which raises exactly this hazard for the full-link case) it wins font matching for weight 400 and the face then lacks every glyph outside "Inter". Inter is the app/token body font (`packages/core/scripts/build-css.ts:98` → `--font-body`) and the default Slides theme font (`packages/slides/src/themes/default-light.ts:20`), so the blast radius is app-wide UI text and Slides canvas text falling back to a system face for the rest of the session. The previous code path (`ensureFontLink`) requested the whole family and could not lose glyphs.

samples.summary: Preview dedupe is keyed on family alone, so a later row needing MORE glyphs reuses a too-narrow subset
samples.evidence: `if (findPreviewFontLink(family)) return;` ignores `text`. The two callers pass different text for the same family: the picker passes the row label only (`font-family-picker.tsx:125`, e.g. "Lobster"), while the dialog row's `textContent` is label + group name (`more-fonts-dialog.tsx:153`, "LobsterDisplay"). Open the dropdown and scroll past Lobster, then open "More fonts…": the existing 7-glyph subset short-circuits the request, and the group-name characters absent from it (D, i, p, a, y) render from the fallback face inside a string that is supposed to be one family — the exact mixed-face artifact this feature exists to avoid. A union/extend (or keying the marker on the requested text) is needed.

samples.summary: Recents rows for full-library families carry no weights, so previews of families with no 400 cut request an invalid weight and stay in fallback
samples.evidence: `data-font-weights={entry?.weights}` uses `CATALOG_BY_FAMILY`, built from the *curated* `FONT_CATALOG` only (line 46). A family picked from the "More fonts…" dialog's full library (e.g. `UnifrakturCook`, weights "700", `font-catalog.full.ts:1816`; `Buda`, weights "300", `:261`) becomes a recent whose entry is undefined, so no attribute is emitted; `ensurePreviewFontLink` then also finds no `CATALOG_INDEX` entry and `previewWeight(DEFAULT_WEIGHTS)` yields `400` (font-catalog.ts:185). css2 answers `family=UnifrakturCook:wght@400` with HTTP 400, and because the marker link is already in the head the per-family dedupe blocks any retry — the row is stranded in the fallback face, precisely the failure the `previewWeight` docstring claims to prevent.

samples.summary: A loaded subset face can satisfy FontRegistry's `document.fonts.check`, marking the family 'loaded' without loading it or firing the re-layout listeners
samples.evidence: `FontRegistry.ensureFont` short-circuits on `document.fonts.check('12px "X"')`, whose default probe text is a single space. Subsets built from row labels that contain a space ("Open Sans", "Nanum Gothic", …) include U+0020, so once the preview face has painted a DOM row it is `loaded` and, when no full link for the family exists yet, it is the face that matches the probe. `ensureFont` then sets status 'loaded', skips `document.fonts.load` and never notifies listeners, so the docs/slides canvas measures and paints the family with a face holding only the picker label's glyphs and no re-layout is ever triggered. Before this change every preview link was a full family load, so a positive `check` implied the whole family really was available.

samples.summary: `previewWeight` can return a multi-weight string, and requesting only the lowest cut makes bolder preview rows synthetic
samples.evidence: `return first || DEFAULT_WEIGHTS;` returns `'400;700'` (two cuts) whenever the first `;`-separated token is empty, contradicting the function's "single weight" contract. Separately, taking only the first cut means the dialog's selected row (`font-medium`, more-fonts-dialog.tsx:243) has no 500/700 face in the subset and is rendered with a synthesized weight, unlike the pre-change full-family load.

verdict.reason: Verified every element of the claim in-repo. ensurePreviewFontLink (font-catalog.ts:217-240) gates only on SSR, webFont:false, entry.eager, findFontLink, and findPreviewFontLink; findFontLink (font-catalog.ts:123-131) matches exclusively on link[data-wafflebase-font], so it cannot see the app-shell stylesheet at packages/frontend/index.html:10-13, which loads Fraunces, Inter:wght@400;500;600;700 and JetBrains Mono in full and carries no such attribute. All three families are curated entries without eager (font-catalog.data.ts:30, :64, :66 — eager:true appears only at :6-15 and :49), so neither line 225 nor 226 short-circuits. The path is reachable in ordinary use: font-family-picker.tsx:250-251 renders a data-font-row for every curated entry and the observer at :112-139 calls ensurePreviewFontLink(family, row.textContent, weights) on first intersection (more-fonts-dialog.tsx:147-162, 236 likewise), appending css2?family=Inter:wght@400&text=Inter&display=swap to document.head after index.html's link with no unicode-range. The docstring at font-catalog.ts:206-210 itself articulates this exact cascade hazard (later-declared subset removes glyphs) but guards only wafflebase-injected links, and the test suite mirrors that partial view (ensure-font-link.test.ts:145-157, 162-166) with no case for shell-loaded families. Impact is app-wide: Inter backs --font-body (packages/core/src/tokens/typography.ts:5, snapshot build-css.test.ts.snap:11) and the default Slides theme (packages/slides/src/themes/default-light.ts:20). No guard, caller filter, or scope argument makes this unreachable; it is a real missing-guard/broken-invariant bug squarely in the correctness lane.

verdict.reason: The quoted short-circuit does exist (packages/docs/src/view/fonts.ts:302), but the claimed harm path does not exist in this repository: FontRegistry is never instantiated in any production code. Repo-wide grep for `FontRegistry` (excl. node_modules) yields only the class itself (fonts.ts:278), its re-export (packages/docs/src/index.ts:188), a test that only calls getFontStatus (packages/docs/test/view/fonts.test.ts:63), and comments/markdown — there is no `new FontRegistry()` anywhere in src. The single would-be call site, packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:351-354, optional-chains through a field that does not exist (`store.fonts?.ensureFont?.(family)`), and its own comment (lines 342-344) says "DocStore does not currently expose a `fonts` registry". I verified that: DocStore (packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:11), MemDocStore (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:32) and YorkieDocStore (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:549) contain no `fonts` member. Therefore ensureFont is never invoked, no onFontLoaded listener is ever registered (fonts.ts:285 has no callers), and no canvas ever consults this status map. Moreover, the docs canvas re-layout on font load is driven independently by document.fonts 'loadingdone' plus fonts.ready in packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2668-2692, not by FontRegistry listeners, and the slides paths (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/apply-font-family.ts:28, pdf-actions.ts:31-35) call ensureFontLink/document.fonts.load with no check() short-circuit at all. The described "docs/slides canvas paints a label-only subset face and never re-lays out" outcome is therefore unreachable; at most this is a latent flaw in an exported-but-unused API, not a blocking correctness defect.
